title: Shadowbox Studios, LLC v. DeKalb County, Georgia (Data Center Moratorium Takings Suit)
jurisdiction: Superior Court of DeKalb County, Georgia
amount: Lawsuit cites more than $30 million invested in the project and alleges the moratorium cut the property's value by as much as $200 million
summary: Shadowbox Studios and affiliate Henrico 183 sued DeKalb County, Georgia on August 5, 2026, alleging the county's moratorium on new data-center applications unlawfully blocks a data center project on their roughly 200-acre site at 3600 International Park Drive, after planning staff had represented the use was permitted there. The suit seeks a declaration that the moratorium is invalid as applied to the property, permission to build, 'just compensation' for the alleged taking, and attorneys' fees.
significance: The case tests whether informal planning-staff representations that a use is permitted can support a takings claim once a moratorium later blocks that same, already-represented project, a theory with growing appeal to developers caught by the nationwide wave of local data-center moratoria. Municipalities that rely on staff correspondence to manage developer expectations without clearly disclaiming legal effect may find that correspondence used against them once a freeze intervenes.
